answer: A loss floor and a buffer (also called a shield) limit losses in different ways. With a 10% floor, your loss is limited to 10% even if the index falls by more—for example, a 12% index drop would mean a 10% loss to the annuity contract value. With a 10% buffer, the insurance company absorbs the first 10% of the index loss; if the index falls 12%, the contract value would lose 2%. These examples are before any contract adjustments, such as surrender charges. Check the contract to understand how its protections and other terms apply.
